senses.meaning: Hạm đội lớn (tàu chiến); đoàn phương tiện quy mô lớn
examples: The Spanish Armada was defeated by the English fleet in 1588.
An armada of warships was deployed to the disputed waters.
A vast armada of aid ships set sail for the disaster zone.

note: Gốc tiếng Tây Ban Nha. Thường viết hoa khi chỉ hạm đội Tây Ban Nha năm 1588.

senses.meaning: Thuộc về đạn đạo (quỹ đạo bay của đạn/tên lửa); (informal) nổi giận dữ dội
examples: The ballistic missile can travel thousands of miles.
The country tested a new intercontinental ballistic missile.
He went ballistic when he found out about the missing funds.

note: 'Go ballistic' (informal) = nổi giận bùng phát (mạnh và đột ngột).

senses.meaning: Nhập ngũ, gia nhập quân đội; tranh thủ/kêu gọi sự giúp đỡ
examples: He enlisted in the army shortly after finishing high school.
She enlisted the help of her colleagues to finish the report.
Thousands of young men enlisted during the first week of war.

senses.meaning: Lựu đạn
examples: The soldier pulled the pin and threw the grenade into the bunker.
A smoke grenade was used to provide cover during the retreat.
The bomb disposal team safely detonated the grenade.

note: 'Grenade' gốc tiếng Pháp/Tây Ban Nha, từ 'granada' (quả lựu).

senses.meaning: Về mặt quân sự, từ góc độ quân sự
examples: The country is militarily powerful but economically weak.
The conflict cannot be resolved militarily — only through diplomacy.
Militarily speaking, the operation was a success.

senses.meaning: Chiến binh, phần tử hiếu chiến (thường có hành động cực đoan)
examples: Several militants were arrested in the border crackdown.
The group was designated a terrorist organisation after a series of attacks by its militants.
The peace talks excluded leaders of the more extreme militant factions.

senses.meaning: Hiếu chiến, cứng rắn (trong niềm tin hoặc hành động)
examples: The union took a more militant stance on the pay dispute.
Militant protesters blocked the entrance to the factory.
A militant minority within the party pushed for more radical policies.

senses.meaning: Bắn phá, ném bom liên tục; tấn công tới tấp (câu hỏi, lời chỉ trích, quảng cáo)
examples: The city was bombarded for three consecutive days.
Reporters bombarded the minister with questions after the press conference.
Consumers are constantly bombarded with advertising online.

senses.meaning: Cuộc bao vây (quân đội vây một địa điểm để buộc hàng); cuộc tấn công kéo dài
examples: The medieval city fell after a three-month siege.
Police laid siege to the building after the hostage-taker barricaded himself inside.
The siege of Leningrad lasted nearly 900 days.

note: 'Under siege' = đang bị bao vây/bị áp lực dữ dội (cả nghĩa đen lẫn nghĩa bóng).

senses.meaning: Đầu đạn (phần mang chất nổ/hạt nhân của tên lửa)
examples: The missile was fitted with a nuclear warhead.
International inspectors are monitoring the number of active warheads.
The warhead was successfully defused by the bomb disposal team.

senses.meaning: Hạm đội (tàu chiến/tàu thuyền); đội xe, đội phương tiện
examples: The naval fleet departed at dawn.
The company operates a fleet of 200 delivery vans.
The battle reduced the enemy fleet to a handful of ships.

senses.meaning: Kho vũ khí; bộ sưu tập vũ khí/công cụ; đội bóng đá Arsenal
examples: The army's arsenal included tanks, artillery, and fighter jets.
The country's nuclear arsenal is one of the largest in the world.
She brought her entire arsenal of arguments to the debate.

note: Nghĩa bóng: 'an arsenal of' = kho đồ sộ (kỹ năng, lập luận...).

senses.meaning: Đình chiến, ngừng bắn tạm thời (hai bên đồng ý)
examples: A truce was called on Christmas Day during World War I.
The two sides agreed to a temporary truce to allow aid convoys to pass.
The uneasy truce between the rival factions broke down after a week.

note: Khác với 'ceasefire' (lệnh ngừng bắn chính thức): truce thường có tính tạm thời và không chính thức hơn.

senses.meaning: Bộ binh (binh chủng chiến đấu trên bộ)
examples: The infantry advanced through the forest under heavy fire.
Thousands of infantry soldiers were deployed to the border.
Infantry units bore the heaviest losses in the battle.

senses.meaning: Khải hoàn, chiến thắng vẻ vang; thành tựu lớn lao
examples: The general's triumph was celebrated with a parade through the capital.
Winning the championship after ten years was a personal triumph.
The peace agreement was hailed as a triumph of diplomacy.

senses.meaning: Giành chiến thắng vẻ vang; chiến thắng (đối thủ hoặc nghịch cảnh)
examples: Good triumphed over evil in the end.
She triumphed despite all the obstacles put in her way.
The underdog team triumphed over the reigning champions.

senses.meaning: Hoạt động gián điệp, hoạt động tình báo bí mật
examples: He was arrested on charges of industrial espionage.
The Cold War was defined in part by intense espionage on both sides.
The novel is a gripping tale of espionage and betrayal.

senses.meaning: Tiêu diệt hoàn toàn (người, loài động vật, hoặc sâu bọ)
examples: The regime attempted to exterminate an entire ethnic group.
Pest control services were called in to exterminate the cockroach infestation.
The disease all but exterminated the rabbit population.

senses.meaning: Vụ thảm sát, sự tàn sát số lớn người (thường thường dân không có khả năng tự vệ)
examples: The massacre of civilians shocked the international community.
Survivors of the massacre testified at the war crimes tribunal.
The My Lai massacre remains one of the darkest moments of the Vietnam War.

senses.meaning: Thảm sát; (informal) đánh bại hoàn toàn
examples: Thousands of civilians were massacred during the siege.
The home team was massacred 8–0 in the final.
His arguments were massacred by the opposition in the debate.

senses.meaning: Cướp bóc, đi cướp phá (đặc biệt là trong chiến tranh hoặc bạo loạn)
examples: Marauding bandits terrorized the villages along the border.
Armed groups marauded through the countryside, looting and burning.
The invaders marauded across the region for months before being repelled.

senses.meaning: Chiến thuật, cơ động quân sự; hành động khéo léo/khôn ngoan; cuộc tập trận
examples: The general's flanking manoeuvre caught the enemy off guard.
It was a clever manoeuvre to outmanoeuvre the competition.
NATO conducted large-scale manoeuvres near the eastern border.

senses.meaning: Điều khiển (xe, tàu) khéo léo; xử trí khéo léo để đạt mục tiêu
examples: She manoeuvred the car into the tight parking space.
He manoeuvred himself into a position of power over several years.
The ambassador manoeuvred carefully to avoid a diplomatic incident.

note: Tiếng Anh Anh: 'manoeuvre'; tiếng Anh Mỹ: 'maneuver'.

senses.meaning: Cuộc đột kích, tấn công bất ngờ (quân sự hoặc cảnh sát)
examples: The commando raid destroyed the weapons depot.
Police conducted a raid on the suspected drug house.
The air raid sirens sent people rushing to their shelters.

senses.meaning: Đột kích, tấn công bất ngờ
examples: Special forces raided the terrorist hideout at midnight.
Police raided several properties in the early-morning operation.
She raided the fridge at midnight for a snack.

senses.meaning: Pháo đài nhỏ, công sự phòng thủ (tạm thời hoặc độc lập); nơi cố thủ
examples: The soldiers defended the redoubt for three days against repeated assaults.
The hilltop redoubt gave defenders a clear view of approaching troops.
The city became a final redoubt for the resistance forces.

note: Nghĩa bóng: 'last redoubt' = thành trì cuối cùng.

senses.meaning: Trận pháo kích liên tiếp; loạt (câu hỏi, chỉ trích) dữ dội
examples: The infantry advanced under a barrage of artillery fire.
She faced a barrage of questions from reporters after the announcement.
The minister was subjected to a barrage of criticism from opposition MPs.

senses.meaning: Cuộc ném bom, pháo kích dồn dập
examples: The city withstood three months of constant bombardment.
Aerial bombardment reduced much of the town to rubble.
The bombardment of civilian areas was condemned by international observers.

senses.meaning: Ngụy trang (che giấu bằng cách hòa vào môi trường xung quanh)
examples: The soldiers wore camouflage to blend into the forest.
The stick insect's natural camouflage makes it almost invisible.
The friendly tone was camouflage for his hostile intentions.

senses.meaning: Ngụy trang, che giấu
examples: The tanks were camouflaged with branches and nets.
She tried to camouflage her nervousness with a confident smile.
The true cost of the plan was camouflaged in the small print.

note: Gốc tiếng Pháp. Ẩn dụ rộng: che giấu ý định/cảm xúc thực.

senses.meaning: Pháo binh (binh chủng); súng pháo cỡ lớn
examples: Artillery fire pounded the enemy positions throughout the night.
The sound of artillery could be heard fifty kilometres away.
The army deployed heavy artillery to break the defensive lines.

senses.meaning: Tội ác man rợ, hành động tàn bạo (nhất là trong chiến tranh hoặc xung đột)
examples: The war crimes tribunal documented numerous atrocities committed during the conflict.
Witnesses described the atrocities carried out by the occupying forces.
The atrocity shocked the world and prompted international intervention.

senses.meaning: Lệnh ngừng bắn (thường được đồng ý giữa các bên xung đột)
examples: A ceasefire was announced after weeks of intense fighting.
Both sides agreed to a temporary ceasefire to allow medical evacuations.
The ceasefire held for three months before hostilities resumed.

senses.meaning: Đẩy lùi (cuộc tấn công); gây ghê tởm, kinh tởm
examples: The defenders repulsed three separate assaults on the fortress.
The invading force was repulsed with heavy casualties.
The graphic images repulsed even hardened journalists.

note: Hai nghĩa: (1) quân sự: đẩy lui cuộc tấn công; (2) cảm xúc: gây ghê tởm.

senses.meaning: Đạn dược, vũ khí và trang bị quân sự
examples: The factory was converted to produce munitions during wartime.
A shipment of munitions was intercepted at the border.
Munitions experts carefully defused the unexploded bomb.

note: Thường dùng số nhiều ('munitions'); 'munition' (số ít) ít gặp hơn.

senses.meaning: Sự ngừng lại, chấm dứt (hoạt động quân sự hoặc bất kỳ hoạt động gì)
examples: Both sides called for an immediate cessation of hostilities.
The cessation of bombing allowed aid workers to enter the city.
The doctor prescribed nicotine patches to help with smoking cessation.

note: Formal. 'Cessation of hostilities' = ngừng chiến sự — cụm từ rất phổ biến trong ngoại giao.

senses.meaning: Sức răn đe (khả năng ngăn chặn đối phương bằng đe dọa phản công)
examples: Nuclear deterrence was the cornerstone of Cold War strategy.
The increased military presence is intended to act as a deterrence.
Whether deterrence alone can prevent conflict is widely debated.

note: 'Nuclear deterrence' = chiến lược răn đe hạt nhân. 'Deterrent' (n/adj) = vũ khí/biện pháp răn đe.

senses.meaning: Hành vi xâm lược, gây hấn; tính hung hăng
examples: The UN condemned the act of military aggression against the neighbouring state.
His aggression on the court makes him a formidable opponent.
Unprovoked aggression is a violation of international law.

senses.meaning: Mang tính trả đũa, nhằm trả thù hay phản ứng lại hành động của đối phương
examples: The country launched retaliatory airstrikes after the border attack.
She feared retaliatory action from her employer after filing the complaint.
Retaliatory tariffs were imposed in response to the trade restrictions.

note: Từ gốc: 'retaliate' (v) = trả đũa. 'Retaliatory strike' = đòn phản công.
